stem: A thin prism $P_1$ with an angle $6^\circ$ and made of glass of refractive index $1.54$ is combined with another prism $P_2$ made from glass of refractive index $1.72$ to produce dispersion without average deviation. The angle of prism $P_2$ is:
solution:
For no average deviation, $\delta_1 = \delta_2$:

$$6^\circ(1.54 - 1) = A(1.72 - 1) \Rightarrow A = \frac{6^\circ \times 0.54}{0.72} = \frac{18^\circ}{4} = 4.5^\circ$$

stem: A flask contains hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio of $2 : 1$ by mass at temperature $27^\circ$C. The ratio of average kinetic energy per molecule of hydrogen and oxygen respectively is:
solution:
$K_{av} = \dfrac{5}{2}kT$ for both diatomic gases at the same temperature.

Ratio $= 1 : 1$

Two radioactive elements A and B initially have same number of atoms. The half life of $A$ is same as the average life of $B$. If $\lambda_A$ and $\lambda_B$ are decay constants of A and B respectively, then choose the correct relation from the given options.
The angular momentum for the electron in Bohr's orbit is $L$. If the electron is assumed to revolve in second orbit of hydrogen atom, then the change in angular momentum will be:
solution:
$L_n = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$. In the first orbit $L = \dfrac{h}{2\pi}$; in the second orbit $L_2 = \dfrac{2h}{2\pi} = 2L$.

Change in angular momentum $= 2L - L = L$.

solution:
Place an identical cuboid on the other side of S to form a cube of side $2L$ with $q$ at its centre, as shown in the figure. Each face of the cube gets $\phi = \dfrac{q/\varepsilon_0}{6}$.

Flux passing through the shaded face $= \dfrac{q}{6\varepsilon_0}$

A $12$ V battery connected to a coil of resistance $6\ \Omega$ through a switch, drives a constant current in the circuit. The switch is opened in $1$ ms. The emf induced across the coil is $20$ V. The inductance of the coil is:
solution:
$I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{12}{6} = 2$ A initially, and $I = 0$ after the switch is opened.

$$\frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} = \frac{-2}{1 \times 10^{-3}} = -2 \times 10^{3}\ \text{A/s}$$

$$e = -L\frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \Rightarrow 20 = -L \times (-2 \times 10^{3}) \Rightarrow L = 0.01\ \text{H} = 10\ \text{mH}$$
